text: Why must interface toolkits be single-threaded?
choices: Because the JVM permits only one thread to hold a native window handle.
A thread-safe widget hierarchy would need locking on every access, would be slow, and would deadlock — every toolkit tried and gave up.
Because Swing components are immutable, so a second thread would have nothing to modify.
Because repainting requires exclusive display access enforced by the operating system.
explanation: AWT was thread-safe, which is precisely why Swing is not. A repaint holding a lock while a handler waits for one is a classic deadlock. Verified: `main` is not the event dispatch thread, and `invokeAndWait` runs on `AWT-EventQueue-0`. The dangerous part is that touching a component from the wrong thread usually appears to work, so it fails intermittently, under load, in ways that do not reproduce.
